question: to the Commission Lena Düpont (PPE) Subject:

Regulation (EU) 2019/21441 introduced mandatory driver assistance systems to improve road safety and protect human life. While these objectives are fully supported, concerns have been raised by emergency organisations that driving during emergency operations may be interfered with by certain driver assistance systems. These interventions may delay emergency services and hinder critical operations. In this context: 1.
Is the Commission aware of reports that mandatory driver assistance systems can interfere with emergency-response driving?
Has the Commission previously assessed whether the current requirements under Regulation (EU) 2019/2144 adequately address the operational needs of emergency vehicles?

Does the Commission intend to introduce or support harmonised exemptions or emergency-response modes, allowing certain assistance systems to be deactivated or adapted during authorised emergency operations?

Regulation (EU) 2019/2144 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 November 2019 on type-approval requirements for motor vehicles and their trailers, and systems, components and separate technical units intended for such vehicles, as regards their general safety and the protection of vehicle occupants and vulnerable road users, amending Regulation (EU) 2018/858 of the European Parliament and of the Council and repealing Regulations (EC) No 78/2009, (EC) No 79/2009 and (EC) No 661/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council and Commission Regulations (EC) No 631/2009, (EU) No 406/2010, (EU) No 672/2010, (EU) No 1003/2010, (EU) No 1005/2010, (EU) No 1008/2010, (EU) No 1009/2010, (EU) No 19/2011, (EU) No 109/2011, (EU) No 458/2011, (EU) No 65/2012, (EU) No 130/2012, (EU) No 347/2012, (EU) No 351/2012, (EU) No 1230/2012 and (EU) 2015/166 (OJ L 325, 16.12.2019, p. 1, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2019/2144/oj). 1
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.8.2026) Regulation (EU) 2018/858 on the approval and market surveillance of motor vehicles1 applies optionally to vehicles designed and constructed or adapted for use by civil protection, fire services and forces responsible for maintaining public order2. Ambulances are defined as special purpose vehicles and specific requirements are provided for them in Annex II, Part III, Appendix 1 to this Regulation. Ambulances are not exempted from the advanced safety systems mandated by the General Safety Regulation (EU) 2019/21443 like advanced emergency braking, emergency lanekeeping, intelligent speed assistance and driver drowsiness and attention warning systems, as they can still benefit from the safety potential of the systems when driven outside the emergency-response regime. However, drivers remain in control of the vehicle at all times and can always override the systems that are meant to assist them. In addition, the legislation provides the possibility to switch off the systems at each trip. The Commission is not aware of any specific issues with mandatory driver assistance systems fitted in ambulances during emergency-response driving. In 2027, the Commission will evaluate the safety systems mandated under the General Safety Regulation and will make a legislative proposal to amend the technical requirements, if needed.
1 OJ L 151, 14.6.2018, p. 1, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2018/858/oj. 2 Article 2(3) of the above Regulation.
